question: Why does the Jetson's Vulkan RPC worker die on 17 blocks of a qwen35 hybrid but not on 16?

evidence_before.crash: SIGSEGV (apport signal 11; WORKER_EXIT 139) on every 17-block middle share of Qwen3.8-27B Q3_K_M (blocks 10-26, 2,922 MiB, no head), 4 of 4: the 2026-09-28 cell (Pi 4 host), r1 (laptop host, Pi 5 tail), r2 (under gdb), b1 (laptop-loopback tail). pp16/tg4.
evidence_before.backtrace: r2 under gdb: libnvidia-eglcore.so.32.7.6 (NVIDIA Tegra Vulkan driver) <- vkAllocateDescriptorSets <- ggml_pipeline_allocate_descriptor_sets <- ggml_vk_matmul <- ggml_vk_mul_mat_q_f16 <- ggml_vk_build_graph <- ggml_backend_vk_graph_compute <- rpc_server::graph_compute; faulting load from x0+8, x0 = 0x28
evidence_before.memory_accounting: Jetson drop = its model buffer + 88-106 MiB at k = 12-17; the engine charges blocks + 44 MiB + one repaid block tensor (58 MiB) + KV

hypotheses.GRAPH: a limit on the number of descriptor sets one graph needs (ggml-vulkan grows pools of 256 sets as a graph is built): it depends on the number of qwen35 blocks in the Jetson's graph, not on memory
hypotheses.MEMORY: the driver's own allocation for a descriptor pool fails when free memory is low (~500 MiB), and it segfaults instead of returning an error: it depends on MemAvailable, not on the graph

m1_9b_k17.what: Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M, the Jetson holds blocks 10-26 (17 qwen35 blocks, the same indices and layer kinds as the crashing 27B cell) = 2,214.6 MiB; laptop host (blocks 0-9), laptop-loopback tail (27-32 + head)
m1_9b_k17.args: MODEL=/opt/heteroserve/models/qwen3.5-9b-q4_k_m.gguf NGL=24 TS=16.5/7.5 WORKERS='jetson t580' P=16 N=4

m2_27b_k16_hog.what: Qwen3.8-27B Q3_K_M, the Jetson holds blocks 10-25 (16 blocks: the passing graph), with a 160 MiB resident filler process on the Jetson started before the worker, so the lowest MemAvailable lands where k17 crashed (~497 MiB)
m2_27b_k16_hog.args: NGL=56 TS=15.5/40.5 WORKERS='jetson t580' P=16 N=4 HOG_MIB=160

rules: GRAPH is supported if m1 dies of SIGSEGV and m2 runs; MEMORY if m1 runs and m2 dies. Any other outcome supports neither alone and is reported as found. A cell 'runs' when llama-bench exits 0 with its result rows and the worker is alive until it is stopped.

The fix follows the supported hypothesis: GRAPH -> a per-architecture cap on the Jetson Vulkan worker's blocks (16 for qwen35 at the pin); MEMORY -> a larger Jetson reserve. Neither is applied before this is scored.
